body:
ADVISOR RULING (01:40) replacing rework item 4 (no survivors). Good stop. Don't modify session.rs. Use SNAPSHOT ISOLATION instead of a kill guarantee:
a) After install exits, aida copies the trial root and PREFIX into a FRESH snapshot directory the installer never had mounted (no hardlinks or reflinks back to the install dirs, and symlinks copied as links, not followed out of the root). The oracle sandbox mounts ONLY the snapshot (plus the read-only bundle and guards); the install-phase roots are never mounted into it. A surviving install daemon can then only write to dirs the oracle never sees.
b) Oracle HOME/XDG/TMPDIR are fresh and created after the snapshot (item 2 stands), and the guard log channel is unreachable from install dirs (item 3 stands).
c) Best-effort detection: after install, scan /proc for live processes whose cwd/root/exe is under an install-phase root, or which still hold the install's guard fd. Kill what's killable, record survivors_detected: N in the trial record, and mark the trial NOT clean if N > 0. Don't refuse.
d) Test: your fork+setsid daemon reproduction keeps writing to the install root, and the oracle result and clean flag are unaffected by it; survivors_detected >= 1 is recorded.
e) A hard guarantee (--unshare-pid in the confinement helper) is filed as a separate STRICT containment follow-up. Don't do it in this lane.
STORY-1679's consensus sketch is queued for the next advisor seat's signoff.
subject: RULING: #2660 item 4 → snapshot isolation (no session.rs)
